business_scope.primary_industry_name: Assembly of Bionic Companion Robotic Animals with Speech Synthesizers

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Code monétaire et financier (Law No. 2016-1691 of 9 December 2016), EU Directive 2018/843 (AMLD 5), Decree No. 2017-924 of 6 May 2017 establishing the UBO register
ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against French, EU, UN, OFAC, and domestic sanctions/PEP lists using automated tools with annual re-screening

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: French language and Latin alphabet required; company names must comply with French grammar, orthography, and public-order rules
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Trademarks or protected names without authorization
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: File administrative appeal with the greffe du tribunal de commerce within two months of official rejection notice; appeal must specify grounds and may be heard by the commercial court

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Accepted for administrative registration of SAS; must maintain a real French address for tax residency and economic substance purposes
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (estimated 3-5% for standard incorporations without red flags)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company Name Search and Clearance via Greffe

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce): Articles L. 210-1 to L. 210-10 (incorporation, corporate object, registered office); Articles L. 224-1 to L. 224-3 (capital subscription and payment); Articles L. 227-1 to L. 227-20 (Société par Actions Simplifiée); Decree n° 2023-232 (Guichet Unique procedures)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Commercial Court Registry), operating electronically through the INPI Guichet Unique (single formality window)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form M0 electronic declaration filed with the signed Statuts (Articles of Association), the deed of appointment of the Président, the Déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs, the bank certificate of capital deposit, the attestation de parution, and proof of enjoyment of the registered office
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The SAS has no legal minimum capital; the articles freely fix the amount. Where cash contributions are made, at least 50% (or 100% if so provided in the articles) must be deposited irrevocably in a blocked escrow account (compte bloqué) with a French bank or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations; the funds are released to the company only upon issuance of the Extrait Kbis. In-kind contributions are due in full at incorporation and must be valued in the articles.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, at the constitutive meeting of the shareholders of [Company], that the share capital of €[X] be subscribed in full as provided in the Articles of Association and that the cash contributions be deposited irrevocably with [Bank] in a blocked account until the legal personality of the company is constituted. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office be fixed at [Address], within the jurisdiction of the Commercial Court of [City]. RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Name] be appointed Président of the Société par Actions Simplifiée, with full corporate authority to represent the company, open bank accounts, sign contracts, and execute all registration formalities before the Guichet Unique and the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registered-office lease confirmation and blocked escrow deposit of the share capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French commercial bank or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations (CDC)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Finalize the lease agreement (bail commercial) or, if the office is provided free of charge, obtain a signed authorization of occupancy from the owner. Open a temporary blocked account in the name of the company in formation and deposit at least 50% of the cash contributions (or the full agreed amount if the articles so require). Obtain from the bank the attestation de dépôt de fonds (certificat du dépositaire) which is mandatory for the filing.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Association
Copy of the registered-office lease or authorization of free occupancy
Identity documents and AML/KYC forms of the founding shareholders
Bank account opening form for the company in formation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses the account due to beneficial-ownership or AML doubts, provide the corrected ownership chart and KYC details and resubmit; alternatively, deposit the funds with the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations and obtain its depositary certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Articles of Association and constitutive decisions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founding shareholders acting jointly; a notary (acte notarié) if the contributions include real property or registered in-kind assets
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Have all founders sign the final Statuts, physically or by qualified electronic signature. Attach the minutes recording the first board resolution (share subscription, registered-office adoption, and appointment of the Président). Ensure the corporate object expressly covers the design, assembly, and commercialization of interactive bionic pet robots, speech-synthesizer toys, and accessories.
required_dossiers: Signed Articles of Association executed by all shareholders
Minutes of the constitutive meeting / first board resolution
Acceptance letter of the appointed Président
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a founder refuses to sign, obtain a written refusal and adjust the shareholding accordingly before publication; if the corporate object is too narrow, amend the Statuts by unanimous written resolution prior to filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the legal notice (avis de constitution) in a Journal d'annonces légales
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A legal announcements newspaper (JAL) approved by the Préfecture of the département of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and publish the avis de constitution indicating the corporate form (SAS), company name, corporate object, share capital, registered office, duration, identity of the Président, and the trade and companies register number (RCS) to be assigned. Collect the attestation de parution issued by the JAL.
required_dossiers: Completed avis de constitution form
Final project of the Articles of Association (supporting document)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the JAL rejects the notice for formal errors, correct the company name, capital, or address and republish; obtain a new attestation de parution and preserve the original for the registry verification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Composite electronic filing on the Guichet Unique (Form M0) with the beneficial-owner declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet Unique Électronique — INPI (single formality window); verification delegated to the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload on the official portal (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) the scanned Statuts, deed of nomination of the Président, Déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs, attestation de parution, bank certificate of capital deposit, proof of registered-office enjoyment, and identity documents of the shareholders and officers. Pay the state filing fee online and track the case in the RNE workspace.
required_dossiers: Form M0 electronic declaration
Signed Articles of Association
Bank certificate of capital deposit (attestation de dépôt de fonds)
Legal notice publication certificate (attestation de parution)
Proof of registered-office enjoyment (lease, free occupancy authorization, or ownership deed)
Déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs
Identity documents of shareholders, Président, and any authorized signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Greffe issues a request for completion or a rejection notice, remedy each identified defect (e.g., inconsistency between the Statuts and the avis, missing page numbering, or divergent capital figures) and resubmit under the same RNE case number; definitive rejections require a new M0 with fresh documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of the Extrait Kbis and release of the blocked capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce of the jurisdiction of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon validation, the Greffe assigns the RCS/SIREN number and issues the Extrait Kbis, the official registration certificate. Present the Kbis to the bank to release the blocked funds into the definitive corporate bank account. Verify that the Kbis correctly records the legal form (SAS), corporate name, capital, registered office, corporate object, and the appointed Président.
required_dossiers: Validated application tracking number from the Guichet Unique
Identity document of the filing applicant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If issuance is delayed, request from the Greffe a certificate of registration or the draft Kbis; any material error in the Kbis is corrected by a rectification request to the registry, supported by the relevant original documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration labor, tax, and market-conformity clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: URSSAF (social security), INSEE (statistical identity), DREETS (labor inspection), and DGCCRF (product safety surveillance)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the Kbis is issued, complete the URSSAF employer registration within 8 days of the first hiring, obtain the SIRET code and the intra-Community VAT number from the tax administration, and prepare the CE technical file and the UE Declaration of Conformity for the bionic pet robots under the Toy Safety Directive 2009/48/EC and the Radio Equipment Directive 2014/53/EU for the wireless AI module.
required_dossiers: Extrait Kbis
SIRET and VAT registration confirmations
CE technical file for the AI pet robot
UE Declaration of Conformity
Workplace risk assessment (DUERP) if staff is employed
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If URSSAF returns the file for an inactive SIRET, request INSEE to resync the enterprise identifiers and resubmit; for a DGCCRF conformity query, submit the technical file, issue corrective product notices, and, if needed, appoint a qualified notified body to re-assess the toy.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Direction Générale des Entreprises (DGE) and DREETS (regional labor and industry directorate) for industrial and workplace supervision; DGCCRF and ANFR for product and radio-frequency conformity of the AI robot
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No separate manufacturing or operating permit is required for the dry assembly of robotic toy pets; the mandatory conformity instruments are the CE marking (self-declaration), the UE Declaration of Conformity under the Toy Safety Directive 2009/48/EC, the Radio Equipment Directive 2014/53/EU (RF module), and the EMC Directive 2014/30/EU.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: DREAL (Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement) under the Préfet de département
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — dry assembly of toys and AI robotic companions does not fall within the ICPE authorization or registration rubriques, and no full étude d'impact (EIA) is required below the thresholds of Article R. 122-2 of the Environmental Code; a Registration-level ICPE file becomes mandatory only if plastic injection molding, metal finishing, or solvent-consuming operations exceeding the legal thresholds are introduced on site.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharged to municipal sewers must comply with the general limit values of the Arrêté of 2 February 1998 (pH 5.5–9.5, suspended solids, zinc, lead, and chromium thresholds); volatile organic compound (VOC) consumption below the directive thresholds is covered by Directive 2004/42/EC reporting; waste electrical and electronic equipment must be handled under the WEEE (DEEE) Directive 2012/19/EU; hazardous substances in the robot components must comply with RoHS 2011/65/EU and REACH Regulation (EC) 1907/2006; batteries must meet Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 with producer-responsibility registration.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification issued by the local fire and rescue service (SDIS) or the commission de sécurité for premises accommodating more than 50 staff members or classified as ERP; structural load inspection certificate for storage racks and mezzanines; occupational workplace clearance delivered by the DREETS labor inspectorate following the submission of the DUERP (workplace risk assessment), the medical-service attestation (médecine du travail) of staff fitness, and the electrical-installation conformity check.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP); online portal: www.impots.gouv.fr; corporate formalities and VAT registration via the Guichet Unique (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a French SAS, incorporate through the Guichet Unique by filing a standard notice (form M0) with the Centre de Formalités des Entreprises; obtain SIREN/SIRET numbers from the French business register (INSEE). After incorporation, the DGFiP assigns an intra-Community VAT number. A non-established foreign entity making taxable supplies in France must apply directly to the Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE) using form 1432-SD (or the non-EU VAT registration form) and appoint an individual tax representative if not EU-established. Identification is subject to verification of legal existence, business activity, and place of effective nexus.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: France does not operate a check-the-box regime. A French SAS is default subject to corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés). No pass-through election is available. Available elections include: (1) group tax consolidation (intégration fiscale) under Article 223 A of the French General Tax Code, subject to a 95% shareholding and intra-group election; (2) the parent-subsidiary regime (régime mère-fille) election for dividend exemption; and (3) for certain SMEs, temporary and limited cash-basis VAT and reduced-rate elections. Hybrid mismatch rules under Articles 212 bis A and following of the General Tax Code constrain cross-border elections; no elective hybrid classification is recognised.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée – TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For established businesses: EUR 85,000 annual turnover for supplies of goods; EUR 37,500 for supplies of services (with lower thresholds for certain liberal activities). For foreign suppliers: no registration threshold applies where taxable transactions are carried out in France; non-established EU suppliers making cross-border distance sales are subject to the EUR 10,000 pan-EU distance-sale threshold with the option of the VAT One-Stop-Shop (OSS).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory B2B electronic invoicing and e-reporting reform will be phased in from 1 September 2026 (large entities) and 1 September 2027 (all taxable persons). E-invoices must be transmitted through a Partner Dematerialization Platform (PDP) or the Public Billing Portal; transaction data must be e-reported to the DGFiP data hub. No real-time stamping applies to domestic e-invoices, but certified cash-register systems must comply with NF 525. Export invoices must contain the SIREN/VAT references and export exemption references; digital clearance for export follows the EU customs delivery-automation (DELTA) environment.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A 0% VAT rate (export exemption with right to deduct input VAT) applies to supplies of goods physically exported from the European Union to a destination outside the EU, provided the exporter is the taxable person and the goods leave EU territory under the conditions of Article 262-I-1° and Article 72 or 74 of the French Customs Code. Also zero-rated are dispatches of goods to another EU Member State when the customer is identified for VAT and a recapitulative statement is filed. Services, including software or robotic-AI toy maintenance services, supplied to a recipient established outside the EU are zero-rated where the service is directly linked to exported goods or to goods placed under a suspension regime (Article 259 A of the General Tax Code). Exemption needs adequate commercial and transport evidence.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (via DELTA-D or one-line declaration; SAD/DAU number)
Bill of Lading (B/L), Air Waybill, CMR or other transport document evidencing physical export
Inward Remittance Certificate (bank credit mandate evidencing receipt of the export proceeds from the foreign customer)
Commercial invoice and sales contract (including Incoterms and payment terms)
Proof of exit from EU customs territory (e.g., customs acknowledgement, EX1 electronic export confirmation)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The French tax administration will claw back improperly claimed export zero-rating, together with input VAT recovered, upon failure to produce the full substantiation bundle within the statutory retention period. Penalties: (1) 40% fine, increased to 80% for bad faith or fraudulent behaviour; (2) late-payment interest at 0.2% per month; (3) a 5% late-payment penalty after 30 days; (4) criminal tax fraud sanctions of up to EUR 500,000 fine and 5 years imprisonment for the legal representative; and (5) seizure and payment blocking for confirmed fraudulent export schemes.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France, acting within the Eurosystem under the authority of the European Central Bank; foreign-exchange, payment-services, AML, and cross-border reporting rules are also administered or enforced by the French Treasury, the Autorité de contrôle prudentiel et de résolution, the Autorité des marchés financiers, and the French customs authority, Direction générale des douanes et droits indirects.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France uses the euro and has no general foreign-exchange control, capital-control, repatriation, or mandatory profit-conversion regime. Current-account payments, including imports, exports, royalties, dividends, interest, and service fees, are generally freely transferable subject to sanctions, AML, tax, customs, transfer-pricing, withholding-tax, corporate-law, and beneficial-ownership controls. Capital-account transactions, including foreign direct investment, intercompany loans, acquisitions, and capital reductions, are generally unrestricted but may require statistical, prudential, investment-screening, or sector-specific filings. Dividends may be remitted after approval of annual accounts, determination of distributable profits, satisfaction of creditor and corporate-law requirements, and application of any required withholding-tax documentation. A French SAS should retain board or shareholder resolutions, approved financial statements, dividend vouchers, tax-clearance evidence where relevant, and related-party pricing support. Transactions involving sanctioned parties, prohibited jurisdictions, unusual payment chains, cryptoasset providers, or high-risk counterparties may be delayed, rejected, frozen, or reported.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France has no statutory requirement to surrender export proceeds to the Banque de France, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no general statutory deadline for converting or repatriating foreign-currency export receipts. Export proceeds may generally be retained in foreign-currency accounts or converted into euros at the company's discretion, subject to contractual payment terms, accounting requirements, tax compliance, customs and Intrastat or statistical reporting where applicable, sanctions screening, and bank AML review. Cash or bearer negotiable instruments physically entering or leaving the European Union at amounts of EUR 10,000 or more must be declared to customs. Banks may impose contractual evidence, invoice, shipping, customs, or source-of-funds requirements before crediting or converting export receipts.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole S.A. and the relevant Crédit Agricole regional banking entity
Groupe BPCE, including Banque Populaire and Caisse d'Epargne commercial banking entities

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account and, subject to entity acceptance, Capital Escrow Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for payment collection and operating payments; Low to Medium for incorporation capital and primary treasury banking. A regulated European Economic Area payment institution or electronic-money institution may provide payment accounts, euro transfers, cards, and foreign-currency services but is not a deposit-taking bank unless separately licensed as a credit institution. An EMI account should not be treated as a substitute for a French bank capital-deposit certificate unless the notary, registry, and incorporation bank expressly accept it. Availability depends on passporting, French regulatory status, safeguarding arrangements, sanctions policy, source-of-funds evidence, permitted countries, and the provider's risk appetite. Offshore digital EMIs without an EU passport, French establishment, or clear cross-border service rights create elevated account-freeze, onboarding, consumer-protection, and payment-finality risks. Stripe may support merchant acquiring or payment processing but does not replace a corporate current account or statutory capital escrow account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French law does not generally require all directors to appear physically at a bank branch for corporate-account opening. Remote onboarding may be permitted where the bank can verify identity using compliant electronic identification and complete beneficial-owner, management, activity, source-of-funds, and expected-transaction checks. In practice, banks may require a video interview, certified identity documents, a French correspondence address, proof of operating substance, wet-signature or qualified-electronic-signature documents, or an in-person meeting for non-resident shareholders, complex ownership chains, high-risk jurisdictions, unusual business models, or capital deposits. A capital escrow account is normally opened before SAS registration using draft constitutional documents and then converted or released after delivery of the registration extract and proof of incorporation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Incomplete or opaque beneficial-ownership chain, nominee ownership, bearer instruments, or inability to identify every person controlling the SAS.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current articles of association; shareholder register or capitalization table; ownership chart to each natural-person ultimate beneficial owner; passports or national identity documents; residential-address evidence; signed beneficial-owner declaration; French beneficial-owner filing evidence where applicable; corporate extracts for all shareholder entities; and powers of attorney.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholder, director, or beneficial owner with no clear French operating rationale or no verifiable management address.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Business plan; French registered-office and operating-address evidence; lease or domiciliation agreement; director appointment documents; customer and supplier contracts; hiring or outsourcing plan; website and product materials; tax-registration evidence; projected French and cross-border payment flows; and explanation of the group's French commercial purpose.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Artificial-intelligence, robotics, hardware, or dual-use concerns causing uncertainty about product classification, export controls, safety, or the true commercial activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed product description; bill of materials; technical specifications; software and hardware architecture summary; end-use and end-customer policy; EU product-compliance roadmap; applicable CE, electromagnetic-compatibility, radio-equipment, machinery, battery, toy-safety, and cybersecurity assessments; export-control classification; sanctions-screening procedure; and supplier documentation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected high-volume card acquiring, marketplace receipts, refunds, chargebacks, international sales, or payment flows inconsistent with the stated low-risk profile.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Twelve-month transaction forecast by currency, country, channel, and counterparty; merchant-acquiring agreement; Stripe or processor onboarding approval; website terms and conditions; refund and chargeback policy; customer-identification and fraud controls; sales invoices; logistics model; tax treatment; and reconciliation procedures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large initial shareholder loan or capital transfer from an unrelated foreign account, especially through multiple jurisdictions or an offshore financial institution.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Shareholder or intercompany loan agreement; board and shareholder approvals; bank statements showing originating funds; audited or management accounts of the funding entity; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds memorandum; transaction rationale; transfer-pricing support; sanctions screening; and evidence that the remitting account is held in the funder's own name.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, politically exposed person, adverse-media, tax-evasion, corruption, or high-risk-country screening alert.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent identity verification; beneficial-owner declarations; sanctions and PEP screening results; certified corporate records; explanation of any false positive; tax-residence certificates; source-of-wealth evidence; litigation and adverse-media clarification; and written compliance escalation through the bank's designated process.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Request for cash-intensive services, cryptoasset-related receipts, third-party payments, unexplained transfers, or payments lacking a clear commercial invoice.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written prohibited-activity policy; approved payment matrix; invoice and purchase-order samples; counterparty verification procedure; bank-account ownership checks; no-third-party-payment undertaking; transaction-monitoring controls; and documented rejection and escalation procedures.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route paid-in share capital to the SAS capital escrow account from an account held in the subscriber's or shareholder's verified legal name. Use SEPA Credit Transfer for euro payments and SWIFT MT103 or ISO 20022 equivalent for non-euro payments. State the precise legal purpose, such as paid-in share capital, share premium, shareholder loan, or intercompany funding; identify the SAS, remitter, ultimate beneficial owner, and incorporation or financing reference; and avoid unexplained third-party remitters. Provide the bank with draft articles, capital-subscription schedule, shareholder resolutions, loan documentation where applicable, source-of-funds evidence, and the notary or bank instructions. After registration, provide the Kbis or equivalent registration extract, final articles, and capital-deposit certificate instructions for release or transfer to the operational account. For non-euro wires, specify EUR conversion instructions, OUR or SHA charge allocation, and correspondent-bank details. Maintain accounting separation between equity, share premium, loans, trade receipts, and customer funds. Record any required Banque de France, statistical, tax, or foreign-investment reporting and retain payment evidence for audit and transfer-pricing purposes.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant Credit Transfer for eligible euro suppliers and beneficiaries; use SWIFT MT103 or ISO 20022 cross-border payment messages for non-SEPA currencies and jurisdictions. Use commercial documentary letters of credit, preferably an irrevocable and, where required, confirmed Commercial LC, for higher-risk suppliers or large equipment purchases. Documentary collections, open-account payments, bank guarantees, and supplier-finance facilities may be used according to counterparty risk. Match each payment to purchase orders, invoices, customs records, transport documents, and sanctions screening. For imports from outside the European Union, reconcile payment data with customs declarations and import VAT records. Define payment approval limits, dual authorization, segregation of duties, beneficiary call-back controls, sanctions screening, duplicate-invoice detection, and daily bank reconciliation. SWIFT MT103 is a payment instruction and is not itself proof of goods delivery; LC document examination and Incoterms allocation must be handled under the applicable UCP 600 or other agreed rules.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable forward contracts with an EU-regulated bank or eligible investment firm, used to hedge documented forecast or committed foreign-currency receivables, payables, intercompany funding, or inventory exposures.

Non-deliverable forwards, where offered by a regulated counterparty and legally available for the relevant currency, used for currencies with convertibility or settlement restrictions; the company must document the underlying exposure, counterparty terms, valuation, collateral, and settlement mechanics.

Currency swaps and cross-currency interest-rate swaps for documented funding or balance-sheet exposures, subject to counterparty credit approval, ISDA or equivalent documentation, margin requirements, EMIR reporting and risk-mitigation obligations where applicable, and accounting designation.
Plain-vanilla currency options and collars for documented commercial exposures, subject to suitability, premium, valuation, disclosure, and corporate treasury authorization controls.

Spot foreign-exchange transactions for operational conversion and settlement. Speculative trading, leveraged products without a genuine underlying exposure, and arrangements that function as unauthorized payment or deposit services should be prohibited by treasury policy.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts (bilan, compte de résultat, annexes) approved by shareholders and filed at the commercial registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce via Guichet Unique / Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholder approval within 6 months of fiscal year-end; registry filing within 1 month of approval. For 31 December year-end: approval by 30 June and filing by 31 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court injunction, administrative fine up to €7,500 for the legal entity, late-filing penalties, and progressive risk of administrative strike-off (radiation) from the RCS for continued non-filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (liasse fiscale – déclaration de résultats n° 2065-SD plus annexes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFIP); required electronic filing in the professional tax area on impots.gouv.fr
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar-year entity: by 3 May of the following year (second working day after 1 May in the official annual calendar). Off-calendar year-end: within 3 months after the close of the fiscal year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 10% of assessed corporate income tax, monthly late interest of 0.20%, 40%–80% penalties for inaccuracies, and increased 100% penalty for fraudulent omission.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation / update of the beneficial-owner declaration (déclaration de bénéficiaires effectifs – DBE) reflected in RCS records
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / RCS via Guichet Unique
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No separate standalone annual deadline; the declaration is deemed confirmed when filing annual accounts, provided no change has occurred. Any share transfer or beneficial-ownership change must be updated within 30 days of the event.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or updating with false information is punishable by a fine up to €7,500 for the legal entity, plus court-ordered regularization and RCS correction orders.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual shareholder decision approving the accounts and granting discharge to the President (procès-verbal d'approbation des comptes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Retained in the company statutory records / minute book; no separate registry filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same 6-month rule from fiscal year-end; must be executed before the annual accounts are deposited with the registry.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to document the decision exposes officers to civil liability, unenforceability of dividend distributions, and aggravated scrutiny by auditors and tax authorities.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor (Commissaire aux Comptes) is mandatory for a French SAS when, at the fiscal year-end, the company exceeds two of the three following thresholds: total balance sheet greater than €4,000,000; net turnover greater than €8,000,000; average number of employees greater than 50. Audit may also be triggered by shareholders, bank covenants, investor agreements, or court appointment even if thresholds are not met.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP (Plan Comptable Général, PCG) as governed by the Autorité des Normes Comptables (ANC); IFRS is applicable only for consolidated accounts of listed groups. The entity may use simplified micro-entity or SME disclosure rules if eligible.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The UBO declaration is deemed confirmed at each annual accounts filing unless a change has occurred. Any transfer or direct/indirect change in ownership exceeding 25% of shares or voting rights, or otherwise affecting beneficial ownership, requires a modification filing with the RCS within 30 days. The company must keep an internal UBO register and ensure the RCS information matches the current shareholder structure before any new shareholder is registered in the company's books.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (registre des mouvements de titres / tableau des actionnaires)
Register of Directors and corporate officers (registre des mandataires sociaux)
Minute Book (registre des décisions et procès-verbaux)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $5,000 – $20,000 per year (if statutory audit applies; $0 if exempt and no voluntary audit)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced rate of 15% on the first EUR 42,000 of taxable profit for small and medium enterprises (SMEs) with turnover below EUR 10 million; Research Tax Credit (CIR) of 30% on eligible R&D expenses up to EUR 100 million; Innovation Tax Credit (CII) for SMEs; tax consolidation regime (intégration fiscale) for groups.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065 (and annexes 2065-A to 2065-SD) filed via the electronic portal 'impots.gouv.fr' (EFI - Echange de Formulaires Informatisés) or through a professional tax filer.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing deadline is the 3rd month following the fiscal year-end (e.g., for a December 31 year-end, deadline is March 31). For non-resident companies without a permanent establishment in France, the deadline is extended to the 15th of the 4th month following year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company identification: name, address, SIREN number, legal form, fiscal year start and end dates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies must provide the name and address of their French fiscal representative and the representative's SIREN number.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income (bénéfice imposable) after deduction of all allowable expenses and application of tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies must report income attributable to their French permanent establishment (PE) or income from French-source activities subject to tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions for tax losses carried forward (déficit reportable) and other adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies may carry forward losses incurred by their French PE, subject to the same limitations as resident companies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of corporate income tax (IS) at the applicable rate, including the reduced rate for SMEs and the standard rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies are subject to the same rates, but the reduced SME rate applies only if the company meets the turnover and ownership criteria and is established in France.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of tax credits (e.g., CIR, CII) and any withholding tax already paid.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies may claim tax credits only if they have a French PE and the credits are attributable to that PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of the tax payable (solde de l'impôt) after offsetting prepayments (acomptes) and credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies must make quarterly prepayments (acomptes) based on the previous year's tax, unless exempt under treaty provisions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of 10% of the tax due, increased to 40% if the return is not filed within 30 days after a formal notice. Interest on late payment (intérêt de retard) of 0.20% per month. Additional penalties for fraudulent filing (80% penalty) and possible criminal sanctions.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 30% (standard rate for dividends paid to non-residents, subject to treaty relief).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim reduced withholding tax under a Double Tax Agreement (DTA), the beneficial owner must submit a certificate of tax residence (TRC) from the foreign tax authority, and complete Form 5000 (or 5001 for dividends) to the French tax administration. The TRC must be presented to the paying entity before the payment date. For EU/EEA companies, the Parent-Subsidiary Directive may allow a 0% withholding tax if the parent holds at least 10% of the subsidiary's capital for at least 2 years.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates: Royalties 33.33% (subject to treaty reduction, often 0% or 5% under DTAs); Interest 30% (treaty rates typically 0% or 10%). For EU/EEA, the Interest and Royalties Directive may provide 0% withholding if conditions are met.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 50 million (annual turnover) for full Master File and Local File; simplified documentation for companies with turnover below EUR 50 million but above EUR 400,000. The threshold for the country-by-country report (CbCR) is EUR 750 million consolidated group revenue.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France applies the 'substance over form' doctrine and anti-abuse rules (e.g., Article 155-A of the French General Tax Code) to counter artificial arrangements. While there is no formal Economic Substance Regulation (ESR) as in offshore jurisdictions, French tax authorities require that a company have real economic activity (employees, premises, decision-making) to benefit from tax treaties and to avoid being deemed a 'shell company' under the EU Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive (ATAD).

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of taxable income, false accounting, or concealment of assets to avoid corporate income tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty of 80% of the evaded tax (majoration pour manœuvres frauduleuses) plus interest; criminal fine of up to EUR 500,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years (Article 1741 of the French General Tax Code).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for the tax debt if they have committed fraud or mismanagement (action en comblement du passif). Travel bans and asset freezes may be imposed. In serious cases, directors face imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Establishing a French SAS with no real economic activity, no employees, no premises, and no business purpose, solely to obtain tax benefits or treaty access.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of tax treaty benefits, reclassification of income, and imposition of 40% penalty for lack of substance. The company may be deemed a 'conduit' and its income reattributed to the ultimate parent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be subject to 'abus de droit' (abuse of law) penalties and personal liability for the resulting tax deficiencies. Travel bans and restrictions on leaving France may be imposed during tax investigations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain or provide transfer pricing documentation, or applying non-arm's length prices in cross-border transactions with related parties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment of taxable income, penalty of 5% of the adjusted amount (up to 40% in case of gross negligence), and interest. In cases of unjustified transfer pricing, a 100% penalty may apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for the additional tax and penalties if they knowingly approved non-compliant transfer pricing policies. In extreme cases, criminal charges for tax evasion may be brought.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to implement AML controls, reporting suspicious transactions, or conducting transactions with sanctioned entities, even if the business is low-risk.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines up to EUR 1 million (or 10% of turnover) and criminal penalties for directors. The company may be blacklisted and lose its ability to operate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face personal fines and imprisonment up to 5 years for money laundering offenses. Travel bans and asset seizures are possible.
